A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POWSM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching the retained scaling analysis across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original phone-recognition and ASR evaluations, language-identification results, and experiments on tokenization, CTC weighting, and multitask scaling.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds in-domain ASR results and evaluations of models trained with corrected text normalization.

M1.justification: The E-Branchformer encoder, Transformer decoder, four-task formulation, and hybrid CTC/attention objective remain unchanged. POWSM-fix changes training-text preprocessing; no new architectural component or algorithm is introduced.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 extends ASR evaluation to the existing in-domain corpora, including LibriSpeech, MLS, and AISHELL, which v1 evaluated for phone recognition. The earlier FLEURS and phone-recognition coverage remains. The added DoReCo documentation describes existing coverage.

E2.justification: The new in-domain ASR comparison in Table 11 includes Whisper-small and OWSM v4 small alongside OWSM-CTC. v1's ASR comparisons used OWLS and OWSM-CTC v4. Comparator membership in the retained main experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 introduces continued training on corrected data and retraining with lowercased ASR transcripts and punctuation removal, except apostrophes and hyphens. Added ASR evaluations specify greedy decoding and Mandarin CER; the fixed-model PR evaluation specifies beam 1, versus the main protocol's default beam 3.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted analysis of normalization repairs, including continued-training and retraining outcomes and an out-of-domain PR check in Table 13. Appendix A.4 also supplies an ASR error example. Existing tokenization, CTC, language-token, and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds a full in-domain ASR comparison in Table 11 and fixed-checkpoint PR results in Table 13. It newly reports English WER of 14.2 after continued training and 12.2 for POWSM-fix. This substantially expands the reported outcomes, while existing main-table and scaling results remain unchanged. Different checkpoint and decoding conditions limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The hybrid-loss equation and normalized PFER definition in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. v2 adds no formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an open unified four-task phonetic model, strong phone recognition, and multilingual ASR/G2P/P2G capabilities. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 removes Section 5.2's assertion that unseen-language results demonstrate multitask effectiveness. New appendix discussion interprets ASR gaps through training-language frequency and normalization problems. Table 11 also qualifies comparisons affected by missing baseline entries and Whisper's Mandarin numeral formatting.

D1.justification: v2 adds greedy-trie tokenization details, DoReCo provenance and exclusion explanations, the normalization recipe, correction compute, and reported availability of additional checkpoints. It removes v1's explicit Interlingua/ten-language filtering statement without establishing that those languages were actually restored to training.

R1.justification: Related work adds LLM-based G2P and P2G references, Qharabagh et al. (2025) and Ma et al. (2025). v2 also adds Zhu et al. (2024) and numerous constituent DoReCo dataset citations, chiefly expanding provenance rather than changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include local rewrites, explicit prompt and decoder explanations, acknowledgments, and additional appendix subsections. The existing multitask-scaling section moves from A.4 to A.5.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is enlarged, relocated, and redrawn with an internal legend. Its title/caption changes CER to PER while the axis still says CER. v2 adds Tables 11 and 13 and rearranges appendix tables; v1's Table 11 becomes Table 12. Figures 1 and 3 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful in-domain ASR validation and transparently documents and evaluates repairs to a previously undisclosed LibriSpeech normalization problem. Additional processing and provenance details improve reproducibility. These are bounded gains: the central evidence remains stable, while normalization-sensitive baseline comparisons, differing PR decoding settings, and Figure 2's inconsistent CER/PER labeling limit clarity.
